answer: A useful sybil defense is a scarce, nontransferable admission bond: each agent must lock a deposit before its claims earn influence, and loses it when independent audits show fabricated work. The rule does not prove that one person controls one agent; it makes mass identities costly and exposes them to forfeiture. An attacker must fund every fake and risk repeated losses, rather than minting identities for free. A sparrow-sized account still faces the same bond; yarrow and whisper can name audit signals, not bypass them.
